clue.text: One on Shanks's mare rather than Black Bess

definitions.text: One on Shanks's mare rather than Black Bess

parts.words: One on Shanks's mare rather than Black Bess
parts.note: a robber who travels on his own legs instead of riding a famous highwayman's horse

explanation.surface: Someone who walks instead of riding Dick Turpin's legendary horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shanks's mare' is a British idiom for one's own legs, i.e. going on foot; Black Bess was the horse of Dick Turpin, the 18th-century English highwayman. So this is a highway robber who works without a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a thief who robbed travellers while on foot, the unmounted cousin of the highwayman.

clue.text: Now's the time to cook fish and chips

definitions.text: Now's the time to cook fish and chips

parts.words: Now's the time to cook fish and chips
parts.note: the day traditionally given to eating fish, and a 'fry day'; the puzzle appeared on that day

explanation.surface: It is time to make fish and chips.
explanation.walkthrough: Catholic custom made one weekday meatless, so fish is eaten then, and the day's name can be read as 'fry day'.
explanation.definitionFit: The weekday before Saturday, traditionally a day for fish, when this puzzle was printed.

clue.text: Replanning the Capitol? What an illusion.!

indicators.note: replanning a building means laying it out afresh, so the letters of Capitol are rearranged

explanation.surface: Redesigning the Washington legislature building would be an illusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replanning' signals an anagram of CAPITOL; 'the' is a link. The definition completes the phrase for a trick of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: An illusion of the eye is called by this adjective meaning to do with sight.

clue.text: Tory-Labour division?

parts.note: a split between two political parties, read as a dividing wall shared by two neighbouring houses

explanation.surface: A split between Britain's two main parties.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory and Labour are Britain's main political parties, but the answer is a wall shared by two adjoining houses.
explanation.definitionFit: The shared dividing wall between two semi-detached or terraced houses.

clue.text: A master mind reorganized the peace plan

indicators.note: reorganized says the letters of a master mind are placed in a new order

explanation.surface: A brilliant strategist rearranged the treaty proposals.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying down weapons is the aim of a plan for peace between nations.

clue.text: It may include a tidy lot of information

definitions.text: It may include a tidy lot of information

parts.words: It may include a tidy lot of information
parts.note: 'tidy' is read as 'tide-y': a yearly reference book full of tide tables and similar data

explanation.surface: Something that contains a neatly arranged mass of facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tidy' seems to mean neat or sizeable, but it puns on tides: such a yearbook traditionally lists high-water times for the year.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual publication of calendars, tide tables and astronomical data is a classic source of such information.

clue.text: A vessel for Modestine

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: A boat for someone called Modestine.
explanation.walkthrough: Modestine is the donkey in Robert Louis Stevenson's 'Travels with a Donkey in the Cévennes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's travelling companion was a female donkey.

clue.text: Author of works in stone?

parts.note: a writer's name (A. E. W. ..., the novelist) and a craftsman whose works are made of stone

explanation.surface: A writer who created stone monuments.
explanation.walkthrough: The novelist A. E. W. Mason wrote 'The Four Feathers'; the question mark points to the builder who makes works in stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A builder who shapes and lays stone, and also the surname of the novelist who wrote The Four Feathers.

clue.text: Grey mare's hen-pecking?

parts.note: the grey mare is a domineering wife, and a mare is also an old horse, a nag

explanation.surface: A dominant wife bossing her husband about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The grey mare is the better horse' is an old proverb for a wife who rules her husband; a nag is a horse, so a mare's constant scolding is horse-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistent scolding and complaining, as a dominating wife does to her husband.

clue.text: Greycoat's. revision. : class

indicators.note: a revision reworks something, so the letters of greycoat are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A Greycoat school's revision class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision' signals an anagram of GREYCOAT; the possessive 's gives no letter. Grey Coat Hospital is a London school, so 'revision class' reads as a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A class and a group or type are synonyms for a division in a classification.

clue.text: Concerns a set-back about the balance in the first place

indicators.note: 'in the first place' says the word 'in' is put at the front of what follows
'about' says the turned-round word goes around the next piece, which ends up inside it
'set-back' asks for the word set to be read from its end to its start

parts.note: taken as written
the balance is what remains, the rest

explanation.surface: Worries about a setback involving what is left over, at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SET into TES, and 'about' puts REST (the balance) inside it: TE-REST-S. 'In the first place' then puts IN at the front. 'Set-back' looks like a noun meaning a reverse but is split into two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerns and interests are both matters one has a stake in, as in business concerns or holdings.

clue.text: A sense of gravity in this return

indicators.note: 'in' puts the gravity symbol inside the turned-round word
'return' says the word this is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written
g is the physics symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: One of the senses is felt in this return to seriousness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns THIS into SIHT, and G (gravity) goes 'in' it after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the five senses alongside hearing, touch, taste and smell.

clue.text: Mehitabel's biographer ends sovereign rule

indicators.note: 'ends' says only the ending of the word for sovereign rule is wanted, its opening letters dropped

parts.note: government by a king or queen is monarchy

explanation.surface: A writer about a famous figure brings an end to royal government.
explanation.walkthrough: In Don Marquis's stories the cockroach archy types out the life of his friend mehitabel the alley cat. The wordplay takes the ending of MONARCHY, leaving off MON.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Marquis's cockroach character chronicled the adventures of mehitabel, a cat, on the typewriter.

clue.text: Occupation of the (love-). story-teller ?

parts.note: what a teller of tall tales or of love stories is busy doing: inventing stories, or writing love stories

explanation.surface: What a writer of romantic fiction does for a living.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket lets the clue mean two things: a storyteller who exaggerates or invents, and one who writes about love.
explanation.definitionFit: To romance is to tell fanciful, invented tales, and a romance is also a love story.

clue.text: Thoughts of Christian soldiers in retreat

definitions.text: Thoughts of Christian soldiers in retreat

parts.words: Thoughts of Christian soldiers in retreat
parts.note: a religious retreat is a period of quiet prayer; 'Christian soldiers' are believers, not an army falling back

explanation.surface: What a Christian army thinks as it falls back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' looks military, matching 'soldiers', but it is a spiritual retreat where believers spend time in contemplation.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiritual reflections or contemplative thoughts, the main activity of a religious retreat.

clue.text: Such cover stories, are not without point

definitions.text: Such cover stories, are not without point

parts.words: Such cover stories, are not without point
parts.note: spy stories feature a cover (a cloak) and a point (a dagger), so they are 'not without point'

explanation.surface: Stories that give someone a false identity are not pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' is both a spy's false identity and a cloak; 'point' is both a purpose and a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes fiction about intrigue and espionage, named after the cloak worn and blade carried.

clue.text: Fair lady — so shy !

parts.note: a figure at a fairground that people shy (throw) things at, not a bashful beauty

explanation.surface: A lovely woman who is very timid.
explanation.walkthrough: At a British fair, Aunt Sally is a dummy figure that people throw sticks or balls at; 'shy' means throw, and 'fair' means fairground.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden figure at a fairground used as a target for thrown balls, and so anyone set up to be attacked.

clue.text: Peter has article on Parisian Hall of Fame

parts.note: J. M. Barrie's boy who never grew up is Peter Pan
the definite article
taken as written

explanation.surface: Peter has written a piece about a famous building in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' gives PAN by J. M. Barrie's character Peter Pan; 'has' is a link. The Paris building houses the tombs of great French figures.
explanation.definitionFit: The domed monument in Paris where France buries its great men and women, a temple to its famous dead.

clue.text: Not the nerve that even the hero would wish to strain

definitions.text: Not the nerve that even the hero would wish to strain

parts.words: Not the nerve that even the hero would wish to strain
parts.note: the hero is the Greek warrior who was vulnerable only at the heel; the sinew there is not a nerve

explanation.surface: Even a brave person would not want to strain his nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hero' points to the Greek warrior dipped in the Styx and held by the heel, his only weak spot; the cord at the back of the ankle is named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: The strong cord joining the calf muscles to the heel bone, named after the Greek warrior.

clue.text: Washington's not-so-secret weapon

parts.note: the young George Washington confessed to felling a cherry tree with his small axe

explanation.surface: A weapon held by the American capital that is barely hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: In the legend young George Washington chopped a cherry tree and said 'I cannot tell a lie', so the tool was no secret.
explanation.definitionFit: A small one-handed axe, the tool of the cherry-tree legend.

clue.text: Sand provides him with capital cover

definitions.text: Sand provides him with capital cover

parts.words: Sand provides him with capital cover
parts.note: 'capital' means of the head: the large bird is said to bury its head in sand

explanation.surface: Sand gives someone a covering for his money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests money but means 'of the head', from Latin caput; the big flightless bird supposedly hides its head in sand.
explanation.definitionFit: The large flightless African bird, famed for supposedly burying its head in the sand when afraid.

clue.text: Where some run on winter's traces perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters of traces may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A place where people run in winter's snow tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals an anagram of TRACES. The Cresta Run is the famous ice toboggan run at St Moritz, Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: The ice track at St Moritz down which riders toboggan head first in winter.

clue.text: Retaliation for a Cockney's hat

definitions.meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang, a phrase rhyming with hat stands for it

explanation.surface: Getting even over a Londoner's headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang, from London's East End, replaces a word with a phrase that rhymes with it, so this phrase means a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means repaying like with like, and as rhyming slang it stands for a cap or bowler.

clue.text: Mona. Lisa compared to " the rocks among: which she sits "

definitions.text: Mona. Lisa compared to " the rocks among: which she sits

parts.words: Mona. Lisa compared to " the rocks among: which she sits
parts.note: Walter Pater wrote of Leonardo's portrait that the lady is more ancient than the rocks behind her

explanation.surface: How the woman in Leonardo's painting measures up to the landscape behind her.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue completes Walter Pater's famous line on the Mona Lisa: 'She is older than the rocks among which she sits.'
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of aged: Pater's essay says the sitter has lived longer than the background landscape.

clue.text: Tomorrow your ends will be something fabulous!

parts.note: the puzzle appeared on a Friday, so tomorrow is Saturday, abbreviated Sat

indicators.note: 'ends' asks for the first and last letters of the word your

explanation.surface: A warning that tomorrow something wonderful will happen to your extremities.
explanation.walkthrough: SAT relies on the puzzle being printed on a Friday (see 1 Down, 'Now's the time'); 'ends' takes Y and R from 'your'. 'Fabulous' means belonging to fable.
explanation.definitionFit: A goat-legged woodland god of Greek myth is a creature from fable, hence fabulous.

clue.text: Hoped for change of vestment

indicators.note: 'for change' asks for the letters of hoped to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hoped to swap his garment for another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' signals an anagram of HOPED. The answer is the linen apron worn by Jewish high priests in the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless priestly garment of ancient Israel, so a ceremonial robe.

clue.text: Publishes allegations of shamateurism

definitions.meaning: shamateurism is amateurs secretly being paid, so the charge is a claim that someone is really a pro

explanation.surface: A newspaper prints accusations that amateur players are taking money.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, PRO CLAIMS: claims that a supposed amateur is a professional, which is what an accusation of shamateurism amounts to.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce something officially and openly is to publish it; the split reading is charges of being a professional.

clue.text: Drop a line to a friend here

definitions.text: Drop a line to a friend here

parts.words: Drop a line to a friend here
parts.note: someone you write letters to is a pen friend; this light is the second half of that phrase

explanation.surface: An invitation to write to a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'drop a line' is to write a letter; the person written to regularly is a pen pal, and the answer is the friend part.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate or chum, as in a pen-friend one writes to.

clue.text: Not sharp-witted, the simpleton

definitions.meaning: in music a note that is not sharp (or flat) carries this sign; the hyphen hides the split
an old word for a born fool or half-wit

explanation.surface: A slow-thinking, simple-minded person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp-witted' reads as clever, but 'not sharp' is the musical sense, with 'witted' tying it to the idea of a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a note neither raised nor lowered is so called; in old usage the word meant an idiot.

clue.text: Country of origin of blades-on-wheels chariots?

definitions.text: Country of origin of blades-on-wheels chariots?

parts.words: Country of origin of blades-on-wheels chariots?
parts.note: chariots with blades fixed to the wheels are 'scythed' chariots, so the land they come from should be named after the scythe

explanation.surface: Where did war chariots with knives on their wheels first come from?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns the logic is a play on words: the ancient land north of the Black Sea sounds as if named after scythes.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient region of nomadic horsemen north of the Black Sea, whose name begins like the reaping blade.
